solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Relate, one way or the other

indicators.note: reading the same in either direction, forwards or backwards, describes a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone is told to relate a story whichever way round it goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole wordplay is the remark 'one way or the other': the five-letter word meaning relate reads identically in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate something to a source is to mention or allude to it, a standard synonym pairing.

clue.text: Order soldiers in advance exercise to make fresh start

indicators.note: the order and soldiers sit inside the exercise word, so 'in' signals containment

parts.note: a recce is a reconnaissance, the scouting exercise done in advance of an attack
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
men is a common word for soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: A commander orders troops into a preliminary drill so the campaign can begin anew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command but is the Order of Merit; a recce is military slang for scouting ahead of an advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin again after a stop is to restart, the plain meaning of this verb.

clue.text: Fish is starter — starter for lunch brought in

indicators.note: the letter is carried into the middle of the other word, signalling an insertion

parts.note: a founder starts, or establishes, an organisation

indicators.note: the starter for a word is its opening letter, here taken from lunch

explanation.surface: A menu lists fish as the first course, with a starter for lunch served too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' first means FOUNDER, one who starts something; 'starter for lunch' then gives L, which goes inside. The menu picture makes 'starter' look like a course.
explanation.definitionFit: A flounder is a flatfish found in coastal waters, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Lady president, one of two in something flowery

parts.note: Rose is a woman's name, so a lady can be Rose
Bush is the surname of two US presidents, father and son, so either is one of the two

explanation.surface: A first lady, wife of one of two presidents, is pictured among flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: George H. W. Bush and George W. Bush were both US presidents, hence 'one of two'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub bearing roses is a plant covered in blooms, loosely described as something flowery.

clue.text: Manages hard American groups

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencil grades
US stands for United States, so American
bands are groups, of musicians or people

explanation.surface: Someone runs tough American gangs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manages' as a verb: to husband resources is to manage them thriftily.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband money or supplies is to use them carefully, a sense of managing economically.

clue.text: Hound knight kept in shed

indicators.note: the knight is held inside the shed word, so these words signal containment

parts.note: a hut is a simple shed
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A dog guards a knight's horse stabled in an outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: To hound someone is to pursue them relentlessly, so it is a synonym of chase down.

clue.text: Scandinavian dish that's spicy and cold

parts.note: a balti is a spicy curry dish popular in Britain
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A Nordic meal is described as both hot-tasting and chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: A BALTI is a curry cooked and served in a metal bowl, a staple of British curry houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea bordering Sweden and Finland is associated with that Nordic region, so loosely Scandinavian.

clue.text: Absence of wickedness in one seeking to be religious

parts.note: no means none, an absence of something
vice is wickedness or immoral conduct

explanation.surface: A would-be monk or nun is notable for having no sinful habits.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a probationer in a religious order, someone not yet professed as monk or nun.

clue.text: 'Scum' — ultimately obnoxious

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads "'Scum' — ultimately obnoxious (4)": the blog parses S (end of obnoxious) + LAG (criminal), but no word for criminal is in the held clue, which appears cut short.

clue.text: Former Labour politician, fellow not best pleased

parts.note: cross means annoyed, not best pleased
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: An old Labour MP is described as a man in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Crossman was a Labour cabinet minister in the 1960s, known for his diaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Crossman served in Harold Wilson's governments, a figure from British political history.

clue.text: Going off after short time, running

indicators.note: the decaying word comes after the time letter, so 'after' orders the charade

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
going off means decaying, as food rotting

explanation.surface: Food spoils quickly while someone hurries along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going off' looks like departing, but it means food decaying.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving at a jog or brisk pace is a kind of running, at a horse's or person's gait.

clue.text: Making a protest, start to slash barriers

parts.note: railing against something is complaining bitterly about it

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here taken from slash

explanation.surface: Demonstrators begin to hack at the fences.
explanation.walkthrough: To rail is to protest angrily, so RAILING is making a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Rows of fence posts with bars form barriers, keeping people out or in.

clue.text: Vehicle of writer unserviceable, dumped by motorway

indicators.note: the writer and unserviceable pieces are placed next to the motorway letters, which go in front

parts.note: M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI in crosswords
a nib is the writing point of a pen, standing for the writer

explanation.surface: An author's broken-down van is abandoned beside the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; crosswords write the 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bus seating a dozen or so passengers is a type of road vehicle.

clue.text: Bird with shining body descending on fish

indicators.note: in a down clue the star sits above and comes down onto the fish, so it goes first

parts.note: a star is a shining heavenly body
ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A bird with gleaming plumage swoops down to catch a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A starling is a common songbird with glossy speckled plumage.

clue.text: Dear Parisian among idiots who may look skyward?

indicators.note: the French word is placed among the idiots, inside them

parts.note: twits are foolish people
cher is French for dear, what a Parisian would say

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's darling is surrounded by fools gazing upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Twitchers are dedicated birdwatchers, who often scan the sky, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen birdwatchers spend time peering up at the sky for rare species.

clue.text: Femme fatale used absurdly long hair to ensnare Conservative

indicators.note: the outer letters trap the Conservative inside them, signalling containment
used absurdly means its letters are rearranged in a silly way

parts.note: a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: A temptress used her long locks to trap a Tory politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurdly' scrambles only the word used; the Tory initial is then trapped between that and the lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A femme fatale is an alluring woman who leads men astray, a temptress.

clue.text: Country dinner earl organised to back ex-PM

indicators.note: the rearranged letters stand behind the ex-PM in support, coming after it

parts.note: Lord North was British prime minister during the American War of Independence

indicators.note: the dinner and earl letters are organised into a new order

explanation.surface: A dinner arranged by a peer supports a former prime minister of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord North was prime minister from 1770 to 1782, losing the American colonies; 'to back' means the scrambled dinner and earl follow him.
explanation.definitionFit: This part of the United Kingdom is often called a country or province.

clue.text: First appearance on stage brings delight

definitions.meaning: an actor's coming on stage is their arrival, how they come in
to delight is to enchant or charm, a verb sense

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently, stressed on the first syllable for coming on and on the second for charming.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an actor's arrival on stage; the other is the verb meaning to charm or enchant.

clue.text: Weapons of a specialised unit — a US soldier's carrying one

parts.note: the SS was the elite Nazi paramilitary unit

indicators.note: the soldiers' word holds the extra letter inside, so carrying signals containment

parts.note: GI is a US soldier, and with the 's it becomes GIS
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: An elite squad's arms are spears held by an American trooper.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'a' is A, then 'carrying' puts another A ('one') inside GIS. Assagais are slender iron-tipped southern African spears.
explanation.definitionFit: Assagais are light throwing spears used in southern Africa, so they are weapons.

clue.text: Inspiring part of hospital accommodation lacking nothing

parts.note: ENT, ear nose and throat, is a hospital department

indicators.note: the accommodation word goes without the nothing letter, signalling removal

parts.note: housing is accommodation
O is the zero shape, nothing

explanation.surface: A hospital unit's housing short of nothing could be called inspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking nothing' reads as complete, but it means the zero letter is dropped from the accommodation word.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking with great excitement that fires others up is inspiring them, loosely enthusing.

clue.text: Plant needing good financial management?

definitions.meaning: a sea pink, a coastal flower with pink blooms

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that one word covers both a flower and frugality.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a pink coastal flower and the virtue of spending money carefully.

clue.text: A Parisian is getting on, achieving complete agreement

parts.note: un is French for a, what a Parisian says
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Frenchman getting older finally finds everyone in full accord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link here; 'getting on' looks like ageing but only ON is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in unison is to act together in perfect concord.

clue.text: Worker noticing things old boy missed

indicators.note: the old boy letters are missed out, removed from the start

parts.note: observant means quick to notice things
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: An employee is good at spotting things that a former pupil overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' looks like part of the old boy's story but signals OB is dropped from OBSERVANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant is an employee who works in a household, so a kind of worker.

clue.text: Initial change made to wedding vehicle

indicators.note: a substitution is made to the wedding word, its first letter replaced

parts.note: a marriage is a wedding

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter, here taken from change

explanation.surface: At first a change was made to the bridal car.
explanation.walkthrough: The initial of 'change', C, replaces the M at the front of MARRIAGE. 'Initial change' reads as an early alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: A carriage is a horse-drawn coach, a wheeled vehicle often used at weddings.

clue.text: Church work must be cut

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A church's composition must be shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To chop is to cut with sharp blows, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Old country lake rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Water levels in an ancient land's lake are going up.
explanation.walkthrough: Eire was the official name of Ireland in the mid-twentieth century, now an old name.
explanation.definitionFit: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland, used officially in older English contexts.

clue.text: Metal pieces, now rare, I repaired

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: I've mended iron goods, which are now hard to find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges NOW RARE I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironware is goods made of iron, such as pots and tools, so metal items.

clue.text: Inventor of peg attached to plate

indicators.note: the peg is attached after the plate, joining the two pieces

parts.note: a paten is the plate used for bread in the Eucharist
a tee is the peg a golf ball rests on

explanation.surface: Someone invented a peg fixed to a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: PATEN is a church plate; TEE is the golfer's peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A patentee holds a patent, typically the person who invented the thing protected.

clue.text: Moves very gradually or stops, avoiding maximum speed!

indicators.note: the word avoids the speed letter, dropping it

parts.note: ceases means stops
c is the speed of light, the fastest possible speed

explanation.surface: Someone inches forward or halts, never hitting top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link. c, the speed of light in physics, is the universe's speed limit.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease something is to move it carefully and slowly, as when easing a car into a space.
